source: 上外版选择性必修第一册 Unit 3 同主题完形(选拔队员/极夜生活/驾艇求救/雪夜行军/重返象岛/写给少年探险者)。用词限本单元/初中/常见词,答案唯一,与阅读/听力关不撞文章。答案位由 _balance 打散。

passages.title: Choosing the Team
passages.text: Before any great expedition can begin, a leader must (1)____ the right people. When Shackleton planned his trip, hundreds of men wrote to him, all (2)____ to join. He could not take everyone, so he had to be very (3)____. He did not only look at how strong a man was. He also wanted to know whether someone could stay (4)____ in danger and work well with others. A team that argues will soon (5)____ apart. Each man chosen had a clear (6)____ to do, such as caring for the dogs or cooking the food. Shackleton believed that a happy crew had a better (7)____ of staying alive. He even valued men who could sing or tell jokes, because laughter helped people (8)____ the long, dark days. In the end, the men he picked were not only (9)____, but also kind and patient. That careful choice was one (10)____ why so many of them came home alive.

passages.title: Living Through the Polar Night
passages.text: For weeks the sun did not rise at all, and the men lived in (1)____ darkness. The cold was so (2)____ that breath turned to ice on their beards. To pass the time, they read aloud, played cards, and (3)____ stories of home. Keeping busy was important, because too much (4)____ time made the danger feel even worse. Every day someone had to break the ice to find fresh (5)____ to drink. The dogs needed feeding, and the boats had to be (6)____ from the moving ice. Shackleton made sure that each man kept a daily (7)____, so that nobody felt useless. He knew that a person who has nothing to do soon loses (8)____. When a small problem appeared, he dealt with it (9)____, before it could grow into a real disaster. Slowly, the days began to lengthen again, and a thin line of light returned to the (10)____. Hope came back with the sun.

so bitter (cold) 刺骨地冷。
shared stories 分享故事。
too much free time 太多空闲时间。
fresh water to drink 可饮用的淡水。

passages.title: The Open-Boat Journey
passages.text: There was no hope of (1)____ on the lonely island, so Shackleton decided to sail for help. He chose five men to go with him in a tiny (2)____ only seven metres long. The sea in that part of the world is among the most (3)____ on the earth, with waves as tall as houses. Day and night the little boat was (4)____ by huge waves, and freezing water poured over the men. They were always wet, always cold, and could hardly (5)____. To find their way, the captain used the sun whenever the clouds (6)____ for a moment. One wrong turn could mean they would never (7)____ land at all. After about two weeks of this terrible (8)____, they finally saw the dark shape of the island ahead. Even then, the rough sea would not let them (9)____ for two more days. When at last they stepped onto the rocks, they could hardly (10)____, but they were alive.

the clouds cleared 云散开(才能用太阳定位)。

passages.title: Marching Through the Night
passages.text: Once on the island, the men still had to cross high mountains to (1)____ the whaling station. They had almost no food and no (2)____ to sleep in. To stop and rest for long would be (3)____, because anyone who fell asleep in the cold might never wake. So they kept walking, hour after (4)____ hour. The ground was covered in deep snow, and thick fog made it hard to (5)____ the way. Sometimes they slid down icy slopes, hoping they would not fall off a cliff in the (6)____. Their bodies were so tired that every step took great (7)____. Yet the thought of their friends waiting for help gave them the (8)____ to go on. After about thirty-six hours, they (9)____ heard the sound of the station whistle far below. That sound told them their long march was nearly (10)____, and help was finally close.

passages.title: Going Back for the Others
passages.text: Reaching safety was not the end of Shackleton's story. Twenty-three men were still (1)____ on the cold island far away, and he had promised to bring them home. Three times he tried to sail back, and three times the thick ice (2)____ his way. He refused to give up, even when others said it was (3)____. At last a small boat lent by another country managed to break through the ice. As it came close to the shore, Shackleton stood on the deck and began to (4)____ the men one by one. To his great (5)____, every single man was still there, thin and weak but (6)____. Not one of them had died during the long (7)____. The men on the beach cheered and waved when they saw their leader (8)____. After two years of danger, the whole team was together again. Their (9)____ was proof of the trust between a leader and his men, and the world soon learned of their (10)____ return.

passages.title: A Letter to a Young Adventurer
passages.text: Dear friend, you tell me that you dream of one day becoming an (1)____ and seeing wild, distant places. That is a fine dream, but let me give you some (2)____. First, never set out without careful planning. The most exciting trips can quickly turn into (3)____ when people are not prepared. Learn to read maps, to watch the weather, and to look after your own (4)____ in the cold. Second, choose your companions with (5)____. On a hard journey, the people around you matter more than any tool you (6)____. Third, remember that real courage is not the absence of (7)____. Brave explorers feel afraid too, but they keep going anyway. Finally, do not explore only to be (8)____. The best reason to set out is the wish to (9)____ something new about the world and about yourself. If you keep all this in mind, you will (10)____ the unknown with both excitement and care. Good luck, and travel wisely.
